analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free due to missing alias/lifetime protection when assigning to an array dimension from a TMP value that can re-enter userland and mutate globals. In this handler, the RHS tmp zval is inserted/destroyed during assignment, and later the LHS container (op1 var) is unconditionally destroyed via zval_ptr_dtor_nogc(EX_VAR(opline->op1.var)). With the PoC, set_error_handler(closure) and side effects through $GLOBALS create aliasing where a closure object referenced by EG(user_error_handler) is freed during execution (via nested zval/array destruction path), but a stale zval to it remains and is destroyed again at request shutdown, producing UAF in zend_gc_delref. The root bug is unsafe refcount/lifetime handling in this opcode handler under self-referential assignment side effects, not shutdown itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires executing ASSIGN_DIM with TMP RHS and side-effectful expression that invokes the user error handler closure and writes into $GLOBALS (PoC: "<?set_error_handler(function(){$GLOBALS['a']='';})[]=$a[$\xff]='';"). Data flow: fuzzer buffer -> PHP script execution -> ZEND_ASSIGN_DIM_SPEC_VAR_UNUSED_OP_DATA_TMP_HANDLER performs assignment and dtors -> object/array graph is prematurely released while still reachable from executor globals (user_error_handler) -> during php_request_shutdown, zend_shutdown_executor_values calls zval_ptr_dtor(EG(user_error_handler)) on stale freed object, causing heap-use-after-free.
